turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. In you come. We'll try not to keep you long.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): About time. Sat out there ages. I'm shattered.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry about the wait. What have you come in for today?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): The kidney check. And the diabetes. Surgery rang.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'm Lila, his live-in carer. He's been worn out this week, more than usual.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah I'm tired. Can we just get on.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): All right. Let me check I've got this straight. Type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and the blood pressure, all still going?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Years. Umm, don't make a meal of it.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain recently?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): And breathless?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about headaches? I ask because of the blood pressure.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that either.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any swelling of the ankles? The kidneys can do that.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes. They puff up if I've been on my feet.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sometimes, after you've been standing. Can you say when it started?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Last winter, or the one before. I don't know. Err, honestly, don't push it.
[SEG0019] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He can't date it. I see sock marks some evenings, not every night.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): So I'll record swelling some of the time, starting last winter or the winter before, you aren't sure which. No chest pain, not really breathless, and no headaches.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm. Get on with it.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): On the diabetes, any shaky spells, like a hypo?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes. Before lunch, if I haven't eaten.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Only sometimes, and if you miss food. Bowels, any change at all?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No. They're fine.
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, he has been buying painkillers at the chemist. I did warn him off them.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): What did you get?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Neurofen. From the shop. For the knee. Two when it's bad, and yeah I know you said not to.
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): They're the 200 milligram ones. He takes two. I can't always get them off him.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): So that's two of the 200s, 400 milligrams of Nurofen, when the knee hurts. It's ibuprofen, which we'd asked you not to use with the kidneys.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): The knee hurts. It's not... I mean it is sore. I'm too tired for word games.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): I hear you. Your bloods from this week, creatinine is 168, eGFR 34. That's down a bit on last time.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): 34. Brilliant. Just what I needed.

[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): I don't mean you're falling apart. Working impression only: the kidney function has dipped, most likely the Nurofen on top of the diabetic kidney disease. Not proven today.
[SEG0035] person_3 (CAREGIVER): So the neurofen stops?

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stops from today, yes. Ramipril carries on, 5 milligrams every morning. For the knee we'll switch to paracetamol, one gram up to four times a day, and I'll put that on a prescription.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Paracetamol does nothing. Ugh. Fine, do what you want.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's kinder on the kidneys, that's the point. Repeat kidney bloods are booked in two weeks, and I'll see you back here in four weeks.
[SEG0039] person_3 (CAREGIVER): His sugar tablets as well, the metformin, 500 with breakfast and with his tea. I'll bin the neurofen tonight.

[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Carry on with the metformin, 500 milligrams twice a day. Both ankles are a little puffy and they pit. The right knee is tender, not hot, not red. Blood pressure today is 146 over 84, pulse 76.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Ow, steady. Are we done?

[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): To close, then. Diabetes, blood pressure and the kidney disease all stand, creatinine 168 and eGFR 34, ankles swell sometimes but the start is fuzzy, no chest pain, not really breathless, no headaches. Stop the Nurofen, keep the ramipril and the metformin, paracetamol for the knee, bloods in two weeks and back here in four.

spec.situation: Older diabetic with kidney disease on review; creatinine and eGFR read aloud; takes ibuprofen from a shop against advice; ramipril continued, painkiller advice changed.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
